title: Collections-automation market — attributed claim ledger
summary: All 24 claims from the sixteen vendored sources are attributed and confidence-rated: 11 verified facts, 13 inferences. One contradiction is flagged and left unresolved on purpose — two sources disagree about a competitor's pricing plans.

sections.heading: Contradiction: Slatebook pricing
sections.body: “Slatebook stated that list prices will remain unchanged through 2026.” (SRC-006, confidence high) directly conflicts with “A partner said Slatebook plans a twelve-percent enterprise price increase in November 2026.” (SRC-007, confidence low). Both sides stay in the ledger with their confidence levels; the recommendation below does not assume either is true.

sections.heading: Recommendation (medium confidence)
sections.body:
Ledgerly's Collections release compares well on implementation speed — the win-loss review credits it in three of five evaluated deals — while the market outlook supports continued investment in regional controls, which both competitors are shipping.

The open pricing question is the one thing leadership should not act on yet: if the partner briefing is right, a competitor price increase lands in November and changes the positioning window; if the public statement is right, nothing changes. Recommended next step is a direct confirmation pass on that single question before any pricing-adjacent decision. Corpus prices are quoted as market evidence only — the Ledgerly catalog ($49 / $99 / $249) is not affected by anything in this ledger.
